chapter: Los Angeles nightlife: Sheffield, Hamp and the Cotton Club
title: The Culver City Cotton Club and Frank Sebastian
summary: The white-only Cotton Club in Culver City was the place to go by 1923-24, with Caroline Snowden and Les Hite staying for years.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: It's funny, I didn't realize that Hamp was held in such regard as a drummer in those early years.
Oh yes, he was. Oh yes, he was. He could play. One of your good drummers around the Cotton Club... It was the heyday of the Cotton Club at that time, Frank Sebastian's...

That Cotton Club started in the early Twenties, and it was out in Culver City. The top act in there was a girl named Caroline Snowden, that had a chorus, and she could sing and dance. At that time, that was the place to go.
I was going to ask you a bit about the Cotton Club, but for some reason I was thinking it was a bit later. I thought it started about 1928. But it started before that.
So when you were out here with Mutt, playing at the Liberty Dance Hall, the Cotton Club was going.
It started way before that. It was in the heyday, say, like 1923 or '24. See, but only White people patronized the Cotton Club.
But this Frank Sebastian guy, he was from here?

I presume he was. A real handsome guy. I recently... The last time I seen him was with Louis. He was managing a big hotel in Sacramento, and we played for him. And he had a club in this hotel. Town and Country I believe was the name of it.
That club seemed to bring a lot of out-of-town musicians in, used a lot of local musicians, and all kinds of people and entertainers went there.
They more or less kept a band pretty steady.
Floyd Turner worked out there for a while...

Well, they might have come out there for a while. But usually, when a band went in there, they stayed a long time. Just like Caroline Snowden, who was a regular there. She didn't play there for two weeks; she played there for months, for years. And Les Hite had a band out there for years, you see.

Before we get too much into that, I think Blakeney told the story about how that band broke up, and Lionel came to be kept over, and that's when Lionel started... I'm sure Blakeney told that story, since it's for the same organization we're doing it in particular regard to that. But let us get back to you and what you were doing. So you went on this boat trip.
